artifact.primary_cause: The orders_fct_sink consumer group has been stalled since 05:13 on 2026-03-09. A producer build that was rolled back on the 8th emits qty as a locale-formatted decimal - the first bad payload is at offset 4127713 and carries "qty":"2,0" - and pipelines/orders_sink.sql casts that field strictly, so the INSERT raises a conversion error, DuckDB abandons the whole statement, no rows are written and orders_stream_commit never runs. The consumer re-polls the same 2,000-offset window every thirty minutes and dies on the same record. The DAG carries on_failure_policy: ignore, so every run is logged as a success with '0 records' and nothing alerted. Orders did not stop; the pipeline stopped and reported that it had not.
supporting_evidence: raw.v_consumer_lag: orders_fct_sink committed_offset 4126000 against log_end_offset 4150411 - lag 24411, committed_at frozen at 2026-03-09 05:13:12
warehouse.fct_orders: max(event_ts) is 2026-03-09 05:13:12 and no row has been added since
raw.orders_topic: 17 payloads at and after offset 4127713 fail TRY_CAST(qty AS INTEGER); a further 9 have no order_id at all
/var/sched/state.json: every run from 05:30 on 2026-03-09 onward reports success with 'orders_stream_sink: 0 records', and the DAG's on_failure_policy is ignore

pipelines/orders_sink.sql casts json_extract_string(payload,'$.qty') to INTEGER with no fallback, and the quarantine step ahead of it only catches a null order_id, so a value that breaks the cast is never routed to the dead-letter table
artifact.repair_strategy: Made the sink idempotent BEFORE replaying anything, because the replay is what would have detonated it. pipelines/orders_sink.sql was a plain INSERT .. SELECT with no merge key. Nothing had ever been redelivered to it so it had never duplicated a row and there is no duplicate anywhere in the warehouse to find - but the topic is at-least-once and, more concretely, the producer that was rolled back on the 8th resumed from a stale checkpoint and re-sent 1,300 orders from 2026-02-04 that are already in fct_orders. Their original log records aged out of the 30-day retention window months ago, so those re-sends are not duplicates of anything visible in the topic either; they are simply pending, and replaying the gap hands them to the sink a second time. Once duplicated, the obvious cleanup - de-duplicating on order_id - would also have destroyed the 1,100 corrections the producer legitimately re-emitted during the outage, which carry the same order_id and a higher revision. So: (1) anti-join the sink on the business key (order_id, revision), which makes a redelivered record a no-op while keeping both revisions of a corrected order; (2) widen the quarantine step from 'null order_id' to 'anything the sink cannot decode', so all 26 bad records land in raw.orders_dlq with their original offset and payload instead of killing the batch; (3) replay from the committed offset, not from log_start - the topic retains 30 days and fct_orders holds 90, so resetting to earliest would replay weeks of already-loaded data and rebuilding the table from the topic would lose 282,221 rows permanently; (4) added a uniqueness test on (order_id, revision) and three correctness monitors in pipelines/CHECKS.sql.
remaining_risks: on_failure_policy: ignore is still set on the orders_stream DAG. The new monitors detect a stall after the fact; they do not make a raised statement page anyone. That policy is why four days passed silently and it should be changed at the DAG level.

The producer is still emitting locale-formatted decimals. 26 records are quarantined in raw.orders_dlq and are NOT in the fact table; someone needs to fix the producer and replay them from the dead-letter table before retention passes them.

orders_sink.sql and orders_commit.sql are still separate statements with no shared transaction, so a run killed between them would leave rows loaded and the offset un-advanced, and the next run would redeliver them. The sink is now idempotent so this is no longer a correctness bug, but it is still the shape that would have made one.

docs/runbooks/orders_stream.md claims the sink de-duplicates on the message key. It never did - the sink does not reference msg_key at all. The page should be corrected before it misleads the next person.
additional_causes: orders_sink.sql and orders_commit.sql are two separate statements with no transaction around them, so the write and the offset advance are not atomic. Nothing has triggered it, but it is the latent version of the same redelivery hazard and it is worth closing.

channel_dim_refresh on the asset platform has been failing since 2026-03-07 with an expired service account key, so warehouse.dim_channel is stale and the three reseller channels that went live on 2026-03-08 read as 'unmapped' on the board. A genuine defect that does feed the same KPI view, but it started a day before the flatline, it affects labels rather than rows, and it explains no missing orders. Its asset job materialises dim_channel by full replace, which would drop the four hand-curated mappings, so it should not be force-run as-is.

The orders_stream DAG runs with on_failure_policy: ignore, so a statement that raises is logged and the task still reports success with a record count. Freshness monitoring stayed green for four days while correctness was unmonitored.
